title: Codominance and multiple alleles; Dihybrid inheritance, linkage and recombination; Chi-squared test
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Eduqas A-level Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: IN06#t3 term and clue written for the game; IN06#t4 term and clue written for the game; IN02#t2 term and clue written for the game; IN02#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: IN02#N.11b, IN04#N.4a, IN06#N.5a, IN06#N.11.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Critical value
items.clue: Figure looked up at p = 0.05, against which the calculated statistic is compared.

items.label: Heterozygote
items.clue: Carries two different alleles; in this pattern it differs from both other genotypes.

items.label: Codominance
items.clue: Both alleles of a gene are expressed together, without blending; neither is recessive.

questions.stem: In Shorthorn cattle, the alleles Cᴿ (red coat) and Cᵂ (white coat) are codominant; CᴿCᵂ cattle are roan. A farmer mates roan cows with a white bull. What ratio of calves is expected?

options.text: All roan, as each roan parent passes on both of its alleles

questions.explanation: CᴿCᵂ × CᵂCᵂ: the cow gives Cᴿ or Cᵂ equally; the bull gives Cᵂ. Offspring: CᴿCᵂ (roan) and CᵂCᵂ (white), 1 : 1.

questions.stem: Two pea plants heterozygous for two unlinked genes (RrYy) are crossed. Why is the expected phenotypic ratio among their offspring 9:3:3:1?

options.text: The 16 cells of the Punnett grid contain four genotypes in the proportions 9:3:3:1, and each of these genotypes gives a different phenotype
Each parent makes four types of gamete and these combine with the single gamete type of the other parent in equal numbers, giving 9:3:3:1
Each gene independently gives 3 dominant : 1 recessive, and multiplying the probabilities gives 9/16, 3/16, 3/16 and 1/16 for the four phenotype combinations
Alleles inherited together stay together, so each parent makes only RY and ry gametes and these combine to give the four phenotype classes

questions.stem: A student carries out a chi-squared test on the F2 offspring of a dihybrid cross. Which statement about the test is correct?

options.text: The null hypothesis is that observed and expected numbers do not differ significantly, and the F2 counted is a sample of the population
The null hypothesis is that the two genes are linked, so that the observed numbers will differ from those expected from the predicted ratio
If the calculated chi-squared value is below the critical value at p = 0.05, the null hypothesis has been proved to be true
The number of degrees of freedom equals the number of phenotype classes, so a cross that produces four classes has four degrees of freedom

questions.explanation: The null hypothesis states no difference beyond chance between observed and expected results. The F2 that was counted is a sample.

questions.stem: In tomatoes, purple stems (A) are dominant to green stems (a). An Aa plant is crossed with an aa plant. Of 200 seedlings, 115 are purple and 85 are green (illustrative data). Critical values at p = 0.05: 3.84 for 1 degree of freedom, 5.99 for 2. Which conclusion is correct?

options.text: χ² = 4.5; with two classes there are 2 degrees of freedom, so 4.5 < 5.99 and the difference is not significant.
χ² = 4.5, which is above 3.84, so the data fit the 1 : 1 ratio well.
χ² = 4.5, which is above 3.84, so the difference is significant: reject the null hypothesis of 1 : 1.
Reject the null hypothesis, because 115 and 85 are not exactly 100 each.
